title: Consistent Prefix Reads Violation (Uneven Partition Replication Lag)
pattern: Querying causally related entities across distinct partitioned tables or database shards without utilizing coordinated snapshot isolation or transaction-locked version boundaries.
why_bad: In a partitioned database, partitions replicate independently and experience uneven delays [118]. If an observer reads causally dependent items (e.g., a question and its reply, or a state trigger and its outcome) across different lagging partitions, they can witness the effect before the cause [118]. This violates consistent prefix reads (or causal consistency), breaking application logic that assumes basic logical flow [118, 130].
detection: Identify read queries directed to different database partition keys sequentially within the same execution block, where the retrieved data has causal relationships but is not filtered by a single, cluster-wide consistent transaction timestamp.
fix: Utilize global snapshot isolation levels (e.g., RAMP transactions or total order broadcast logging) that ensure causal writes become visible across all partitions atomically [74, 75, 118].
source: Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 5 / passages [118, 130]; Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Chapter 13 (Coordination Avoidance & RAMP) / passages [73, 74, 75].
